away.name: Jacob Fowler
away.news: Jakub Dobes had a breakout 2025-26 season, leading the Canadiens to an impressive playoff run, but his sluggish start to 2026-27 opened the door for Jacob Fowler, who hasn't backed down from the challenge. The 21-year-old Fowler has been outstanding this season and is coming off a 30-save performance (.938 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the Boston Bruins. He has a stellar 2.13 GAA and .926 SV% in 12 games this season (9-1-2). The Canadiens enter Monday's game as -107 road favourites against a New York Rangers team that is 5-1-0 in their past six games.

home.name: Joonas Korpisalo
home.news: Korpisalo has seen limited action since making his debut earlier this month, returning from a lower-body injury, but has been solid when called upon. The 32-year-old Finnish goalie was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 29 of 30 shots (.967 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the Calgary Flames. The Rangers enter Monday's game as slight -101 home underdogs against a Montreal Canadiens team coming off a 4-1 loss to the Colorado Avalanche.

away.name: Nikita Tolopilo
away.news: The Canucks are coming off a rare victory yesterday, courtesy of a strong performance by Leevi Merilainen in a 6-3 win over the Vegas Golden Knights. Now, on the tail end of a back-to-back, the Canucks are turning to the recently recalled Tolopilo for his first NHL start of the season instead of the struggling Kevin Lankinen. The 26-year-old Tolopilo has a 2.52 GAA and .897 SV% in 11 games (7-2-2) with Abbotsford (AHL) this season. The Canucks enter Monday's game as significant +288 road underdogs against the Utah Mammoth, who are on a five-game losing streak (0-2-3).

home.name: Karel Vejmelka
home.news: Sebastian Cossa has given Utah a viable secondary option between the pipes lately, so, surprisingly, the team is turning to Vejmelka, who allowed five goals on 21 shots (.762 SV%) in their previous game, a 6-5 shootout loss to the San Jose Sharks. The 30-year-old Vejmelka has not been reliable lately, allowing three or more goals in seven of his last eight games (1-5-2). Still, the Mammoth enter Monday's game as massive -336 home favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that snapped a seven-game losing streak yesterday with a 6-3 win over the Vegas Golden Knights.
